item.title: Registered Voters Now 100m As INEC Removes 1.6m Invalid Records
item.description: The Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, said it is now managing a verified voter register of over 100 million. INEC ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍⁠​​⁠⁠‌​‌‌​Chairman, Prof. Joash Amupitan, disclosed this in Abuja on Wednesday, during the commission’s meeting with Resident Electoral Commissioners (RECs) from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). The update comes as the Commission said it has selected 17,676 polling units for the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS) mock accreditation and result upload exercise slated for Saturday, 28 November 2026, ahead of the general election in January 2027. According to him, the Commission removed over 1.6 million invalid, duplicated and deceased records from its supplementary voters’ register – the removal has now brought the total verified National Register of Voters from earlier 103 million to more than 100 million citizens. The INEC chairman said that the invalid 1.6 million records were taken off the list, following the application of an Automated Biometric Identification System (ABIS) and statutory claims and objection audit. He noted that no fewer than 11 million people were registered across the three phases of the Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) conducted since 2025, while over 10.77 million new registrants were retained. “Beyond hardware and logistics, we must also account for inclusivity and evidentiary clarity. Following three phases of Continuous Voter Registration (CVR) that added over 10.77 million new registrants and an ABIS and statutory claims-and-objections audit that purged over 1.6 million invalid, duplicate, or deceased records, our verified register stands at over 100 million citizens, including 232,658 Persons With Disabilities (PWDs) requiring accessible polling layouts and assistive materials. “This was before we went into claims and objections. When we activated the claim and objection to the display at the registration areas and also through the internet, we received about 311,000 complaints. “We addressed those complaints and we found that about 232,000 of those complaints were found to be genuine and we’ve been able to address those issues,” he said. INEC Chairman Joash Amupitan Amupitan added that further inquiry from INEC showed that there were an additional 113 which the commission discovered on its own on the supplementary register. He noted that beyond the new supplementary list, most of the complaints received online bordered on anomalies in the existing national register compiled between 2011 and 2023. item.title: Rewane projects 4.5% growth, urges investors to rethink strategies
item.description: By Onome Onyeme The Chief Executive Officer of Financial Derivatives Company, Bismarck Rewane, has projected Nigeria’s economic growth at between 4.3 and 4.5 per cent in 2027, urging investors to rethink traditional investment strategies and embrace emerging opportunities. Speaking at the 23rd edition of the Alpha Morgan Economic Review, held virtually yesterday, Rewane said changing economic realities, technological innovation and evolving business models were reshaping investment decisions globally. “The rules of the past are no longer the rules of the present, definitely not the rules of the future,” he said, urging investors to embrace innovation, research and emerging industries rather than rely on past market performance. Rewane, who examined global economic developments and Nigeria’s investment outlook, said businesses and investors that failed to adapt to changing realities risked losing relevance. He cited the evolution of global businesses, including Apple, as examples of how innovation and leadership could determine corporate fortunes, stressing that past success was no guarantee of future dominance. Rewane observed increasing participation in the capital market, with more companies raising funds through the market rather than relying solely on commercial bank loans. However, he warned of possible property market bubble risks, particularly amid the rapid expansion of construction and property investments in Lagos. Rewane projected that some companies could record revenue growth of between 25 and 40 per cent, driven by capital investment, expansion and increased operations across Africa. He also projected the Naira to trade between N1,500 and N1,600 per dollar in 2027, while anticipating an end to global interest rate increases. He clarified that the projections represented his personal assessment of economic developments. item.title: Five things to expect in 2027
item.description: Things are set to heat up in 2027. From rising temperatures to Democratic control of the US Congress to another total solar eclipse, here are five events to look out for in the coming year. El Nino in a hotter world With an El Nino cycle among the strongest ever observed, 2027 could break new global temperature records. El Nino is a naturally occurring weather phenomenon that emerges from the Pacific approximately every two to seven years. It shifts global rain patterns and brings higher temperatures to much of the planet, exacerbating rising temperatures caused by climate change. This year’s El Nino has already impacted maize in central America, fishery catches in Peru and sugar and rice production in Southeast Asia. But for harvests in some regions and food price spikes, “the worst is probably yet to come,” according to Kaveh Zahedi, of the United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization. And these impacts will hit as farmers are already struggling with higher prices linked to the war in Iran, and with international aid reduced around the world. Democrats and Trump The Democratic takeover of both chambers of the US Congress in January promises to transform the final two years of President Donald Trump’s term, giving his opponents powerful tools to challenge his agenda — but not a free hand to impose their own. After their sweeping November midterm victory, Democrats plan an early push to ease living costs, including restoring Affordable Care Act insurance subsidies, reversing cuts to health care and rolling back Trump’s tariffs. They also want to end the war in Iran, which has driven up fuel prices. Hakeem Jeffries, poised to become the first black House speaker, will oversee a majority able to put Democratic bills to a vote, shape federal spending and use budget negotiations to press for concessions. Perhaps the more immediate impact will come from congressional investigations. Democratic-led committees can subpoena officials and demand documents on alleged corruption, Trump’s family business dealings, immigration enforcement and the conduct of the Iran war. Such scrutiny could trigger lengthy court battles. Democrats could also pursue a third impeachment of Trump, although removing him would require a two-thirds Senate majority — a formidable hurdle. In the Senate, Democrats can block Trump’s cabinet and judicial appointments, including any Supreme Court nominee. But most legislation needs 60 Senate votes to overcome procedural obstruction, and Trump can veto measures that reach his desk. Overriding him requires two-thirds majorities in both chambers. The result could be two years of subpoenas, spending standoffs and confrontation, punctuated by possible deals on shared priorities. French presidential election After 10 years in power, Emmanuel Macron will step down following France’s presidential election, scheduled for April 18 and May 2. item.title: Trump, NATO chief urge Russia not to ‘expand’ Ukraine war
item.description: US President Donald Trump and NATO chief Mark Rutte urged Russia not to “expand the war” in Ukraine, in a joint statement issued Wednesday after meeting in Florida. The “outstanding” and “very impactful” meeting focused on the wars in Ukraine and Iran, said the statement issued by the White House after the closed-door talks at Trump’s Mar-a-Lago resort. “We also discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war, and the importance of obtaining a peaceful resolution to the war as rapidly as possible,” the statement added. The joint appeal by Trump and Rutte comes despite the US leader describing Russian President Vladimir Putin as “my friend” during a meeting in China last week. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has taken issue with Trump’s comments on Putin. “For us, he is a killer,” Zelensky told CNN. Rutte was asked about Trump’s comments in an interview with Fox News’ “Fox & Friends” on Wednesday. “What President Trump is doing, also in the meeting in Shenzhen, is testing Putin,” the NATO secretary general said. “How serious is he? Is he willing to come to the negotiating table? Is he willing to really engage in talks. “So let’s keep the pressure on. I think it is working, and we have to keep that going.” Trump, accused by critics of siding with Moscow over Kyiv, said following his meeting with Putin that the Russian leader wants to see the war end by “diplomatic means.” The Florida meeting comes as European nations have expressed a desire to join preliminary talks that have so far only included Ukraine, the United States and Russia. Rutte said any agreement is going to have to include security guarantees for Ukraine. “When the war ends, either with a peace deal, preferable, or if not possible, a long-term ceasefire, we need to make sure that Ukraine has the security guarantees going forward,” he said. “But the most important thing here,” Rutte added, “is that we have to make sure that Ukraine has what it needs to keep the fight going, being so successful and putting that maximum pressure on the Russians.” Trump and Rutte also discussed increasing defense spending, which the US president has pressed European powers to do, the joint statement said. The Florida talks also came as Pentagon chief Pete Hegseth is expected to announce in coming weeks a review of the US force presence in Europe. item.title: CBN raises BDC’s dollar cash limit to $1m weekly
item.description: Banks to receive dollar cash from apex bank to meet demand By Babajide Komolafe The Central Bank of Nigeria (CBN) has temporarily raised the weekly dollar cash purchase limit for Bureau De Change (BDC) operators from $150,000 to $1 million, as part of measures to address seasonal demand pressures in the foreign exchange market. The apex bank also pledged to supply authorised dealer banks with dollar cash to meet the requirements of their BDC customers, allowing licensed operators to access up to 100 per cent of their foreign exchange purchases in cash. The development was confirmed by bankers and forex dealers who spoke to Vanguard, following an email communication from the CBN on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, outlining the new operational arrangements. Kunle Ezun, Chief Economist, Ecobank Nigeria, confirmed the development, saying: “Very correct. The message was sent yesterday. The banks are putting machinery in place to commence the sale. It will be T+2.” Taiwo Ebenezer, Chairman, Association of Bureaux De Change Operators of Nigeria (ABCON), South-West Zone, also confirmed the directive, saying some banks had already contacted BDC operators. “Yes sir, some banks have been calling. CBN also promised to fund the banks,” he said. In an email dated November 24, 2026, sent by Yasir Shanono Shehu and Aderinola Shonekan, of the CBN, the apex bank said the measures were designed “to address seasonal demand pressures and improve orderly access to US$ cash for end users.” The apex bank stated: “All licensed BDCs (please see attached) may access US$ cash for FX purchased at the NFEM through the Authorised Dealer Banks (ADBs) with which they hold accounts, and the CBN will support ADBs with any cash requirements to meet the demand of their BDC clients.” Under the new arrangement, “the approved licensed BDCs may receive up to 100% of an approved FX purchase in US$ cash from the ADB where they hold their settlement account.” The CBN added that “the weekly purchase cap is temporarily increased from USD 150,000 to a maximum of USD 1 million per BDC.” BDCs are required to submit requests through the BDC FX Purchase Tracker (FXBT), while authorised dealer banks are expected to acknowledge requests same day and confirm or reject them on the portal, stating reasons for any rejection. According to the CBN, “ADBs shall consolidate confirmed cash requirements, which will be validated against the FXBT, after which the CBN will supply US$ cash to the ADBs for onward disbursement to the BDCs.” On settlement, the apex bank said: “Settlement between the CBN, ADBs and BDCs is on a T+2 basis, i.e. two (2) business days after the trade date on which the ADB confirms the request on the FXBT. The BDC’s settlement account shall be debited at the point of cash disbursement.” The CBN, however, said existing documentation and KYC/CDD requirements, the prohibition of third-party transactions and the 24-hour sell-back rule remain in force and apply equally to cash transactions. item.title: Uduere: ‘Their sacrifices won’t be in vain’ – Obi, Kwankwaso visit slain NDC members’ families
item.description: By Jimitota Onoyume, Henry Umoru & Egufe Yafugborhi Presidential candidate of the Nigerian Democratic Congress, NDC, Mr. Peter Obi, has condemned the killings at Uduere community in Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State during Monday’s rally of the party, describing the incident as tragic and unacceptable. Meanwhile, Omo-Agege has criticised the conduct of police personnel deployed to the venue of the rally, alleging that about 50 officers failed to protect members of the party during the attack. Also, the Obidient Movement condemned Monday’s attack, observing that Nigerians can no longer have confidence in a police force that appears more interested in protecting political interests than protecting citizens, stressing that the police derive their authority from the people. Obi said it was disturbing that some people could resort to killing others simply because they want to occupy political positions, assuring the bereaved families that the sacrifices of the victims would not be in vain. “People cannot sacrifice for this in vain. All the sacrifices will not be in vain. We cannot kill or harm people simply because we want to become political leaders,” he said. Obi spoke, Tuesday, night during a condolence visit to the family of the late Moses Anaughe, who was shot dead during the attack. Anaughe, a former member of the Delta State House of Assembly representing Ughelli North Constituency I and former Federal Commissioner of the Federal Character Commission, was attacked by the assailants while stepping out of his vehicle. He was allegedly shot at close range. At the deceased’s residence in Agbarho, Obi consoled his widow and was seen sharing playful moments with their young son in an effort to comfort the grieving family. He was accompanied by the NDC governorship candidate in Delta State, Deacon Oyovwaiye Chris, and the party’s Delta Central senatorial candidate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege. Police came to watch me being executed — Omo-Agege Meanwhile, Omo-Agege expressed disappointment that despite the heavy police presence, the assailants were able to unleash violence on the gathering. He said: “We went to the campaign event with six trucks of policemen deployed to the venue. “We expected protection for everyone at the venue. It never occurred to us that they were merely coming principally to watch me being executed.” Obi, Kwankwaso visit Umukoro’s family The NDC presidential candidate, yesterday, continued his condolence visits alongside his running mate, Senator Rabiu Kwankwaso, with a visit to the family of slain activist in Abraka, Ethiope East Local Government Area of the state, Efemena Umukoro, who was also killed during the party’s campaign rally at Uduere. They were received by the widow, Mrs. Gift Umukoro, and other members of the family. item.title: NLC, TUC feud: How we brokered peace in Ajaero, Osifo’s rift — Obiajulu
item.description: *lSays some individuals exploited situation to tear labour movement apart By Victor Ahiuma-Young The protracted disagreement between the leadership of the Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, and the Trade Union Congress of Nigeria, TUC, over the Federal Government’s N70,000 transport relief agreement with the NLC, which the TUC rejected, threatened to undermine the unity and collective bargaining strength of organised labour. The disagreement escalated into public exchanges and personal attacks between NLC President, Joe Ajaero, and his TUC counterpart, Festus Osifo, raising concerns that the welfare and interests of Nigerian workers were being overshadowed by the leadership crisis. Worried that the feud could further divide the labour movement and weaken its ability to defend workers’ interests, veteran labour leaders, led by pioneer NLC President, Hassan Sunmonu, intervened and brokered peace between the two leaders. Other prominent figures involved in the reconciliation included Dr Peace Obiajulu, Comrades Peter Esele, Ayuba Wabba, Bobboi Kaigama and Quadri Olaleye. In this interview, former TUC President, Dr Obiajulu, recounts what triggered the crisis, how it escalated, and how the intervention of the labour elders helped restore cordial relations between the two labour centres. She reveals that poor communication largely fuelled the disagreement, while some individuals exploited the situation, warning that the crisis nearly tore the labour movement apart and ultimately put workers’ interests at risk. What actually led to the disagreement between the Nigeria Labour Congress and the Trade Union Congress, and how did you get involved in the reconciliation? To start with, I was not even aware that there was a disagreement between the two organisations. I was called by Quadri Olaleye, a former President of TUC. He told me that the President of NLC had asked whether Mrs Obiajulu, whom we fondly call Mummy, had been informed about the meeting. That was when I asked whether there was a problem between TUC and NLC. He said yes. I responded that it was a family matter, just like disagreements between a husband and wife or among children in a family. In all honesty, I do not know who initiated the reconciliation process. I am sure it was the elders. They must have seen what was happening on television and read about it in the newspapers. If I had come across the situation myself, I would equally have reached out to some of the elders to intervene. I would not like to see organised labour become a target of public ridicule. The moment TUC and NLC begin to quarrel or fall apart, workers are left on their own. Whenever there is a problem within the labour movement, workers are the ones who suffer because nobody will be left to speak effectively on their behalf. How serious had the disagreement become before the elders intervened? If there is a disagreement between NLC and TUC, workers ultimately bear the consequences. item.title: Risk of retaining fuel subsidy outweighed political consequences – Idris
item.description: • President misrepresented on electricity supply promise – Onanuga •FG defends power sector reforms, increased revenue to states By Juliet Umeh MINISTER of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, has defended President Bola Tinubu’s economic reforms, saying the removal of fuel subsidy and unification of exchange rates saved Nigeria from imminent economic collapse. Idris, who spoke at an interactive session with journalists organised by the All Progressives Congress, APC, Presidential Campaign Council Media and Strategic Communications team in Lagos, Monday, said the President took politically risky decisions in the overriding interest of the country. He maintained that the reforms had improved government revenues at all levels, strengthened the economy and positioned the country for sustainable growth. He said: “When the President took office in May 2023, there were two major policy decisions. One was doing away with this monster called fuel subsidy. The second was ensuring that the multiple exchange rate regimes that we had in this country were also done away with. “Presidents after presidents, everyone knew that fuel subsidy was a big problem and a big drain on the economy of this country. But no one was able to achieve its removal until President Bola Tinubu came. “It was not a convenient decision for Mr President. In fact, it was politically risky for him, for someone who had just won an election, who had just been sworn in and who had another election staring him in the face.” Idris explained that the administration considered the consequences of retaining the subsidy and concluded that delaying the reforms would have been more damaging to the country. “The risk of waiting any longer far outweighed whatever political risk he, as a person, as a president or as a politician, should take. “This created enough fiscal headroom, not just for the Federal Government but also for the sub-nationals. Federal Government has made a lot more money. Sub-nationals have made a lot more money,” he said. Economy on path to recovery The minister also said international financial institutions and rating agencies had acknowledged improvements in Nigeria’s economic outlook. He said: “The IMF, the World Bank, everybody is saying, yes, we have some challenges as a nation, but our economy is on the path that will lead us to prosperity. “Our GDP is on the rise. Inflation that was becoming a big problem has been curtailed. Headline inflation, food inflation, all are down.” However, journalists at the meeting raised concerns over persistent insecurity, high petrol prices, inadequate electricity supply, distribution of Compressed Natural Gas, CNG, buses and the impact of increased allocations to state governments on citizens’ welfare. item.title: Tinubu vows to sustain peace, defeat insurgency in North-East
item.description: •Promises rescue of abducted Askira Uba schoolchildren •Shettima, Zulum hail security gains, seek second term for Tinubu ABUJA — President Bola Tinubu has pledged to sustain the relative peace recorded in Borno State and the North-East, directing security agencies to intensify operations against fleeing insurgents. Tinubu, who spoke yesterday at an All Progressives Congress, APC, rally in Maiduguri ahead of the 2027 general elections, said the security gains achieved by the armed forces would be consolidated and translated into full economic recovery. In a statement by his spokesman, Bayo Onanuga, the President commended Borno State Governor, Prof. Babagana Zulum, for restoring hope and transforming the state’s economy. “Let me start by thanking the Governor of the State, Prof. Babagana Zulum. Well done on restoring Borno State and transforming its economy. “You restored our hope by believing that stability will bring development,” he said. Tinubu, who commissioned projects including the National Youth Service Corps Female Lodge and Borno International Conference Centre, said the North-East had witnessed economic improvements in the last three years, with increased investments in education, healthcare and infrastructure. He urged fleeing insurgents to surrender their weapons, assuring troops of continued government support and improved welfare for them and their families. On the abducted schoolchildren from Askira Uba, the President promised intensified intelligence gathering and rescue operations. “I think there’s a point to note here: the abducted children of Askira Uba School. They are there, and with our prayers and intelligence, our armed forces will rescue them, Insha Allah,” he said. Attributing the security gains to cooperation among political leaders, residents, the Federal Government and security agencies, Tinubu thanked the people of Borno for their support and commended Vice-President Kashim Shettima for his loyalty. He also acknowledged former governor Ali Modu Sheriff and other North-East political leaders for their contributions. In his remarks, Shettima urged voters to reject the former Vice-President and African Democratic Congress, ADC, presidential candidate, questioning his leadership capacity. “You don’t expect someone who could not provide leadership at home by reconciling his own people to provide leadership at a national level,” he said. Shettima urged the electorate to reward Tinubu’s administration with a second term, claiming it had performed well in Borno, Bauchi, Taraba, Adamawa and other states. Earlier, Zulum thanked Tinubu for his interventions in Borno, saying they had contributed to the state’s recovery and economic repositioning. “If someone has done well for you, like our President, then we should give him a good reward. “We have witnessed relative peace in Borno State and the North-East,” he said. item.title: Tinubu, Peter Obi, Soludo, others mourn as Nollywood legend, Pete Edochie dies at 79
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi, Benjamin Njoku, Vincent Ujumadu & Johnbosco Agbakwuru PRESIDENT Bola Ahmed Tinubu, presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Mr Peter Obi, and Anambra State Governor, Professor Chukwuma Soludo, have expressed deep sadness over the death of veteran Nollywood actor, Chief Pete Edochie, describing his passing as a monumental loss to his community, the Igbo nation, Nigeria and Africa. In separate condolence messages, they described Edochie as a distinguished son of Anambra State and one of Africa’s most celebrated actors, whose exceptional talent and contribution to the creative industry projected African culture and traditions to audiences across the world. Nigeria has lost one of its greatest thespians —Tinubu In a tribute personally signed by him, the President described Edochie, popularly known as Ebube Dike, as a graceful and larger-than-life personality, both on and off the screen. The tribute read: “It was with deep sorrow that I received the news of the passing of Chief Peter Uwadiegwu Ogugua Edochie, better known as Pete Edochie. “Chief Edochie was an exceptional actor and one of the progenitors of our vibrant film industry, Nollywood. He was graceful and larger than life, both on screen and in person. “He was one of Africa’s most recognisable thespians. For decades, he plied his craft, bringing joy, laughter and charm to many homes. “I recall his unforgettable portrayal of Okonkwo in the Nigerian Television Authority adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s evergreen novel, Things Fall Apart, in the 1980s, and his many brilliant performances afterwards. “Through memorable performances in productions such as Igodo, Rituals and Lionheart, he helped shape the evolution and international visibility of Nollywood. “His portrayal of traditional institutions, family structures, African values and the complexities of human relationships helped project Nigeria’s cultural heritage and storytelling traditions to audiences worldwide.” Tinubu added:”Pete Edochie was not only an actor; he was also an administrator, broadcaster and journalist — truly one of our finest. “His place in the pantheon of those who shaped the film industry, our common norms and popular culture remains indisputable. “As I mourn the passing of this legendary actor, I also reflect on his life. Pete Edochie lived well. He played his part and exited gracefully. “In his works, he lives forever. Many generations will talk about the life and work of Chief Edochie in the arts industry and academia, in barbershops and marketplaces, and indeed wherever people gather.” Obi pays tribute In his condolence message, Obi recalled Edochie’s memorable portrayal of Okonkwo in the television adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s Things Fall Apart, noting that the actor’s deep understanding of African culture and command of both English and Igbo distinguished him as an exceptional performer. item.title: 2027: No margin for error, INEC warns RECs, sets 6 operational priorities
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Professor Joash Amupitan SAN, has told Resident Electoral Commissioners RECs that “margin for error simply does not exist” in the conduct of the 2027 General Elections. This was as he set six operational priorities for the RECs, from whom he said he expects “immediate, documented compliance and personal accountability.” Amupitan spoke on Wednesday in Abuja at a strategic consultative meeting with the RECs from the 36 states and the Federal Capital Territory FCT. Reviewing the off-cycle elections since he assumed office in October 2025, Amupitan said the exercises showed “what is achievable when planning starts early, logistics are properly sequenced, and supervision is hands-on.” They covered the governorship elections in Anambra, Ekiti and Osun, the FCT Area Council elections and sixteen legislative bye-elections. He said every bottleneck identified in the off-cycle reviews “must be permanently closed before Saturday’s nationwide simulation and well ahead of January 16.” He cautioned that “general elections operate on an entirely different magnitude and complexity.” The Commission, he said, is managing a verified register of over 100 million voters, including 232,658 Persons With Disabilities who need accessible polling layouts and assistive materials. “In an exercise of that scale, even minor administrative lapses in one state can trigger national headlines and cast doubt on otherwise solid work elsewhere. Margin for error simply does not exist. At this decisive stage of the electoral cycle, the calendar no longer allows for leisurely deliberation or deferred action,” he said. According to him, the Presidential and National Assembly elections will hold on Saturday, January 16, 2027, across 177,299 polling units, followed on Saturday, February 6, 2027, by the Governorship and State Houses of Assembly polls. He described the RECs as “the Commission’s chief operational commanders in the field,” adding that the credibility and public legitimacy of the elections “rest squarely on the precision, vigilance, institutional neutrality, and administrative rigour” with which they lead their state offices. The first priority, he said, is the nationwide mock accreditation and result transmission exercise on Saturday, November 28, 2026, in two polling units per ward. “It is a live operational stress test of our upgraded BVAS devices, our logistics workflows, and our automated result validation safeguards on the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV),” he said, referring to the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System (BVAS). Every REC, he said, must personally oversee state-level preparations and submit “a comprehensive, candid technical audit” to INEC Headquarters by Monday, November 30, 2026. item.title: ‘Five bullets’ — NDC supporter recounts attack on Omo-Agege’s campaign team in Delta
item.description: A supporter of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) has recounted how gunmen allegedly shot him five times during an attack on the campaign team of Ovie Omo-Agege, the party’s candidate for Delta Central, in Uduere, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State. The survivor, who sustained gunshot injuries to his chest and mouth, narrated his ordeal in a video shared on the NDC’s X page on Wednesday. The video showed him speaking from his hospital bed during a visit by Peter Obi, the party’s presidential candidate, and Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, its vice-presidential candidate, to survivors of the attack. Recounting events leading up to the shooting, the man said he had received threats after participating in a 10,000-man march organised by the NDC in Delta State. According to him, his wife received a telephone call from individuals who threatened to shut down his business. “To be very precise, on Sunday, when we were in church, in the early hours of the day, they went and sealed the whole business premises. I could not get access to the premises; I could not offload my goods,” he recalled. “A week later, my truck that brought goods from Lagos, they seized the truck and drove it to the local government secretariat.” He said the truck was detained for more than four days, adding that no explanation had been provided for its seizure. The supporter said the attack occurred on Monday while Omo-Agege was addressing supporters at the campaign venue, when gunmen stormed the gathering and opened fire. He said one of the attackers called out his name before shooting him as he attempted to escape towards his car. “One of them started shouting, ‘That is Agba, shoot Agba, that is Agba, look at Agba going.’ Before I could say Jack, the gunshot came straight to my chest,” he said. “There is a bullet here, through the throat. There is a bullet here…five bullets on the chest and the mouth. “So, the target was just to kill me, but to God be the glory, I’m alive.” He attributed the attack to his political affiliation and support for the NDC’s presidential and vice-presidential candidates. “The whole thing is because I’m supporting NDC; I’m supporting Obi and Kwankwaso,” he said. Another survivor receiving treatment at the hospital also expressed determination to continue supporting the party despite the violence. “No matter the number of persons they shoot or attempt to kill in their time, Peter Obi will become president, Rabiu Kwankwaso will become vice-president, and Nigeria will be okay,” he said. Recall in a statement issued on Tuesday, the Nigeria Police Force spokesperson, Ani Iniedu, said preliminary reports indicated that six people were killed and several others injured during the attack. Iniedu said the police would sanction any officers found to have acted improperly, unlawfully or breached professional standards during the incident. item.title: Tinubu’s transport fare reduction policy
item.description: President Bola Tinubu’s promise to cut transport fares by about 40 per cent is receiving deserved attention, but Nigerians will judge it by its genuine impact on the common people. The target, announced under the National Affordable CNG Transit Programme (NACTP) for 2027–2031, applies only to “participating routes”. Nigerians need a nationwide programme. The package centres on an agreement with Chinese manufacturer Yutong Bus Co. Ltd to supply 300 compressed natural gas buses. The first 100 are expected in Lagos by December 2026; subsequent buses are to be assembled through YP Automobiles at the former Leyland plant in Ibadan. The Presidency says this will support jobs, technical skills and local manufacturing. It also cites 2,000 additional CNG refuelling infrastructure units. The reasoning is simple: cheaper fuel should reduce operators’ costs and, hopefully, fares. But 300 buses cannot transform road transportation in a country of more than 230 million people. Private bus, minibus and taxi owners must not be pushed aside by government-subsidised fleets. Government should offer conversion loans, reliable gas supplies and affordable maintenance. Otherwise, only a few corridors may benefit. Rural transport deserves equal attention. Farmers contend with poor roads, expensive fuel and costly journeys from farms to markets. An urban passenger bus scheme will do little for them. CNG support must reach rural transporters and produce-haulage operators. Feeder roads and market links need investment too. Cheap movement of food is part of alleviating hardship. The timing of this policy is politically awkward. In May 2023, Tinubu announced that the petrol subsidy was gone. The pump price, about N185 a litre, quickly rose above N500; by September 2026, NMDPRA data showed prices around N1,300–N1,450. After three and a half years of hardship, a 40 per cent fare promise ahead of the 2027 elections looks to some like a campaign sweetener. Only sustained implementation can dispel that suspicion. India’s successful PM-eBus Sewa scheme combines private bus operation with public support for depots, charging infrastructure and payment security in its 10,000-bus programme. Brazil’s transport-voucher system requires employers to help meet workers’ commuting costs. Nigeria should explore lessons from these equally heavily populated countries. Nigerians want the Federal Government to publish the Yutong contract details, delivery schedule, routes, fares and funding arrangements. They should set benchmarks, audit savings and penalise operators who receive support without reducing fares. States, unions, private owners, farmers and consumer groups should also be involved. Buses should be properly maintained, with a guaranteed gas supply. These services should be extended to rural areas. item.title: Nigeria Joins Global Pact To Protect Marine Biodiversity, Unlock Ocean Resources
item.description: Nigeria has secured a significant international milestone for the country’s marine and blue economy, following its formal ratification of a landmark United Nations treaty on the conservation and sustainable use of marine biodiversity in areas beyond national jurisdiction. The historic instrument of ratification was deposited on behalf of President Bola Tinubu by Nigeria’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations, Jimoh Ibrahim, at the United Nations Headquarters in New York. ﻿ Speaking at the ceremony, Ibrahim highlighted the economic and strategic importance of the agreement to Nigeria, noting that it would expand the country’s opportunities to benefit from ocean resources through greater participation in the governance of the high seas. The Biodiversity Beyond National Jurisdiction (BBNJ) Agreement, also known as the High Seas Treaty, provides a framework for the protection, management and sustainable use of marine resources in areas beyond national jurisdiction. For Nigeria, a coastal nation along the Gulf of Guinea, the agreement marks a significant step towards strengthening its marine economy, protecting biodiversity, supporting fisheries and unlocking opportunities in emerging ocean-based industries. A major implication of the ratification is Nigeria’s plan to develop a proposal for the establishment of a highly protected marine area on the high seas. The initiative is also expected to strengthen efforts to conserve marine ecosystems while promoting the fair and equitable sharing of benefits from ocean resources, particularly for developing countries. Nigeria signed the BBNJ Agreement on May 3, 2024. Following the deposit of its instrument of ratification, the agreement will enter into force for Nigeria on December 24, 2026. This will enable the country to participate as a full Party at the first Conference of the Parties, scheduled to open on January 11, 2027. At the ceremony, Ibrahim acknowledged Evelyn Campos Sanchez, Officer-in-Charge of the United Nations Treaty Section, for receiving Nigeria’s instrument of ratification. Nigeria’s commitment to the agreement is further reinforced by the establishment of the Federal Ministry of Marine and Blue Economy, alongside the adoption of a National Blue Economy Policy and a national roadmap for implementing the treaty. As a party to the agreement, Nigeria will continue to advocate for the fair and equitable sharing of benefits arising from marine genetic resources and digital sequence information. The country will also push for stronger capacity-building initiatives and the transfer of marine technology to African and other developing nations. Ambassador Ibrahim further noted Nigeria’s support for the establishment and effective operation of a Special Fund with adequate and predictable resources to enable developing countries to implement the agreement. item.title: [VIDEO] 2027 Elections: APC’s Strategy Is To Ensure NDC Candidates Can’t Campaign Nationwide — Olumide Akpata
item.description: A former president of the Nigerian Bar Association, Olumide Akpata, has accused the ruling All Progressives Congress (APC) of plotting to frustrate candidates of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) and prevent them from campaigning across the country ahead of the 2027 general elections. Akpata, who is a chieftain of the NDC, spoke during an interview on Channels Television’s Politics Today while reacting to the attack on members of the party by armed hoodlums in Benin City, ahead of the visit of the party’s presidential candidate, Peter Obi, to Edo State, on Wednesday. He decried the intimidation and hostility shown by the APC against the NDC, saying that two facility owners the opposition party had paid to have their town hall meeting in Benin City refunded the payment when they received calls not to allow the event to hold there. Akpata, who contested the Edo State governorship election in 2024, also recalled how hoodlums invaded his office in the state capital and opened fire. He called on the ruling APC to allow Nigerian voters to decide whether they have done well, rather than resort to violence. While responding to a question about the rig-and-die slogan attributed to the NDC, Akpata said anybody caught rigging should face the full wrath of the law. The former NBA president said that the NDC will not back down in the face of intimidation. He also said that the opposition party would ensure that the matter is not swept under the carpet. “We are not going to sink to the despicable depths these other persons are willing to do,” he added. item.title: FG Launches ₦1.45trn Lagos Ports Modernisation, Targets 48-Hour Cargo Clearance
item.description: The Federal Government has flagged off the modernisation and upgrade of the Lagos Port Complex, Apapa, and Tin Can Island Port. The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, supported by the Minister of Finance and Coordinating Minister of the Economy, Mr Taiwo Oyedele, and other senior government officials, unveiled the project on Wednesday, describing it as a strategic investment that will reposition Nigeria as a leading maritime hub in Africa and strengthen the country’s competitiveness in global trade. Speaking at the groundbreaking ceremony at the Tin-Can Island Port, Oyetola said the project, which would cost £746 million (approximately ₦1.45 trillion), would address decades of infrastructure deficits, reduce logistics costs, attract international shipping lines, stimulate industrial growth and create at least 20,000 direct and indirect jobs. The Minister of Marine and Blue Economy, Adegboyega Oyetola, said the project, which would cost £746 million (approximately ₦1.45 trillion), would address decades of infrastructure deficits (X/@GboyegaOyetola) He said the modernisation programme was a significant step towards realising President Bola Tinubu’s Renewed Hope Agenda, which prioritises infrastructure development as a catalyst for economic growth, investment and job creation. According to the minister, the two ports, which have served as major gateways for Nigeria’s international commerce for decades, have become increasingly inadequate to meet the demands of a rapidly expanding economy and changing global shipping requirements. He noted that Apapa Port, established in 1913, was more than a century old, while Tin Can Island Port was commissioned in 1977 when Nigeria’s population stood at approximately 67.2 million, annual trade was about $17 billion, and cargo throughput was 8.11 million metric tonnes. Today, he said, Nigeria’s population has grown to approximately 240 million, merchandise trade exceeds $100 billion annually, while cargo throughput has increased to 129.3 million metric tonnes, nearly 16 times its 1977 level. Oyetola stressed that the mismatch between growing economic activities and ageing port infrastructure had made comprehensive modernisation both urgent and unavoidable. “The cost of inaction is far greater than the cost of modernisation,” he was quoted as saying in a statement by the special adviser to the minister, Bolaji Akinola, as saying, adding that Nigeria will not surrender its competitive advantage. “Our ambition is to attract more direct calls by international shipping lines, retain Nigerian-bound cargo, expand transshipment opportunities and establish our ports as preferred gateways to trade across the African Continental Free Trade Area. We cannot achieve this ambition with infrastructure that falls behind the demands of modern shipping,” the minister said. item.title: [VIDEO] Insecurity: ‘We’ll Achieve Peace,’ Tinubu Assures Borno Residents, Urges Terrorists To Lay Down Arms
item.description: President Bola Tinubu has promised residents of Borno State that his administration is working to achieve lasting peace in the state. Tinubu, who stated this at the All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential rally in Maiduguri, Borno State, on Wednesday, also assured them that schoolchildren still in captivity will be rescued. The President, who said he was aware that residents were concerned about the security challenges, thanked them for their support, which he said contributed to the successes recorded so far. All Progressives Congress (APC) presidential candidate and incumbent President Bola Tinubu (C) addresses a campaign rally in Maiduguri on November 25, 2026. Photo by AUDU MARTE / AFP He also commended the Nigerian Armed Forces for their sacrifices for the nation. “We will achieve that peace. The terrorism will go. They have the opportunity now to lay down their arms, to lay down all arms and surrender all weapons, change from the character of terrorism and banditry,” he said. Tinubu, however, reiterated his call on registered voters to collect their permanent voter card and cast their votes for the APC in the 2027 general elections. Earlier, Vice President Kashim Shettima urged voters in the state to support the re-election of Tinubu in the January 16, 2027 election. Similarly, Governor Babagana Zulum said residents were witnessing the gradual return of peace to Borno State. He commended the APC-led Federal Government for its support to the state. Zulum assured the President that Borno and North-East residents would vote en masse for him. He, however, appealed for the resumption of oil exploration in the region.
